To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

flow cytometric determination can be used for rapid evaluation of the sensitivity of CRLM cells to TKIs in vivo and that it can be used for the rapid identification of CML patients who are likely candidates for switching to second-line treatment with another TKI.

the flow cytometry-based assay of CRKL phosphorylation in CML patients is a useful method for the rapid evaluation of TKI sensitivity/responsiveness and the identification of patients who may benefit from switching to another TKI.

the flow cytometric monitoring of P–CRKL, and of P-SFK, in CML patients treated with TKIs, provides a reliable and rapid in vitro assay that enables the evaluation of the sensitivity and resistance of CML patients to TKIs, and the rapid identification of those patients who are likely candidates for switching to second-line TKI therapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for the monitoring of the inhibition of P-CRKLand P-SFKin leukocytes from patients treated with TKIs.
the study of the influence of the magnetic field (MF) on the properties of the magnetic field.
the study of the in vitro effect of the TKIs on P-CRKL, P-SFK, and P-ABL1.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the study of the authors is a very good one, but there are some points that should be considered for improvement.
this study is a good example of a flow cytometric approach for the monitoring of BCR-ABl1 kinase inhibition.

this study has demonstrated that flow cytometric monitoring of P-CR KL and P-SFK is a rapid and reliable method for assessing the in vitro sensitivity of BCR-AB L1+ leukocytes to TKI treatment, and that this technique could be used for monitoring TKI sensitivity and/or resistance in routine clinical practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results of flow cytometric analyses correlated well with the results of immunoblotting analyses of the same samples.
the flow cytometric monitoring of P-CRK L and P-SFK in leukocytes from CML patients is an easy, rapid, and reliable method for assessing the sensitivity of leukemia cells to TKIs.
we have developed a flow cytometry-based method for the assessment in vitro of the sensitivity of BCR-ABLL1-positive cells to TKIs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the in vitro inhibition (50% or more) of CRKL phosphorylation in CML patient’s leukocytes is associated with a good response (complete hematologic and molecular remission) to the TKI used.
flow cytometry can be used to monitor the in vitro sensitivity/resistance of BCR-ABLI+ cells to TKIs in patients with CML.
flow cytometric analysis of P-CR KL and P-SFK is a reliable method for assessing the sensitivity of leukemia cells from patients with CML to TKIs.
